stories.headline: Earthquake of 6.9 magnitude hits near Ozernovskiy in Russia
stories.title: Earthquake of 6.9 magnitude hits near Ozernovskiy in Russia
stories.summary: Moscow, Oct 16: An earthquake of 6.9 magnitude struck 76 km northeast of Ozernovskiy in Russia on Friday, the US Geological Survey said. The epicentre, with a depth of 143.2 km, was initially determined to be at 52.01 degrees north latitude and 157.25 degrees east longitude, it said. A perceptible earthquake with an intensity of up to four magnitude points has been registered in Kamchatka, Russia's state-run TASS news agency reported, citing the Kamchatka branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences’ Geophysical Service. “Instrumental intensity in Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky amounted to up to four points,” scientists said. Scientists estimated its magnitude at 6.5 first, but later revised it to 6.9. It was felt as a magnitude-5 earthquake in the region, it said. “According to verified information, the magnitude of this seismic event was 6.9. Its epicentre was located on land, 156 km southwest of Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky, at the depth of 138 km. In Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky, it was felt as a magnitude-5 earthquake,” seismologists said. A number of residents of the region’s administrative centre evacuated from their apartments because of tremors, it said. Inside residential buildings, the earthquake caused light fixtures to swing violently, doors to slam shut, and tableware to rattle. According to eyewitnesses, the tremor, which occurred at 3:36 pm local time (3:36 a.m. GMT), continued for about one minute.

stories.headline: Assam: Akhil Gogoi Ends 14-Day Sit-In After Govt Assures Flood Relief
stories.title: Assam: Akhil Gogoi Ends 14-Day Sit-In After Govt Assures Flood Relief
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: GUWAHATI: Raijor Dal chief and Sivasagar MLA Akhil Gogoi on Thursday suspended his 14-day sit-in protest outside the Assam Legislative Assembly (ALA) after the state government assured him of relief, compensation and rehabilitation for flood-affected families in Upper Assam.
Gogoi began the protest on October 2, demanding compensation for affected families in Sivasagar, Charaideo, Jorhat and Golaghat.
He suspended the agitation after meeting Cabinet ministers Keshab Mahanta and Pijush Hazarika, who visited the site on Chief Minister Dr. Himanta Biswa Sarma's instructions.

Gogoi submitted a memorandum seeking the release of pending Rs 15,000 interim relief payments, additional compensation, fresh surveys to identify excluded beneficiaries and reconstruction of damaged roads and other infrastructure.
He also demanded Rs 10 lakh for each family whose house was damaged or destroyed.

stories.headline: Flood fears rise with flyover plan at Puthukkad in Keralam
stories.title: Flood fears rise with flyover plan at Puthukkad in Keralam
stories.summary: Residents seek pillar-supported structure citing drainage disruption and growing vulnerability to waterlogging
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The proposed Puthukkad flyover on National Highway (NH) 544 in Keralam’s Thrissur has triggered serious environmental and flood-related concerns, with residents warning that the proposed 1.38-km earth-filled approach could turn the highway into a massive barrier to the natural flow of rainwater and aggravate flooding in the low-lying town and adjacent panchayats.
The Puthukkad Melpalam Janakeeya Samithi has demanded that the proposed flyover and its approach roads be constructed on pillars, instead of raising a long stretch of the highway with earth.

According to the project proposal, only about 70 metres at the Puthukkad Signal Junction would remain open at ground level, while nearly 1,380 metres would be built on an earth-filled embankment, points out the Samithi.
It argues that such a structure could obstruct natural drainage between the low-lying areas on either side of the highway.
“Puthukkad is located in a geographically sensitive area where water movement cannot be treated as a secondary consideration.
A long earth embankment could become a physical barrier to the natural flow of floodwater,” said Seby Kodiyan, chairperson of the Samithi.
The concern assumes significance against the backdrop of the region’s history of waterlogging during periods of intense rainfall.

K. K. Aneesh Kumar of the Kerala Sasthra Sahithya Parishad (KSSP) has pointed to the flooding in Puthukkad during the 2018 and 2019 deluges and instances of waterlogging reported during heavy rain in subsequent years.
When the Peechi dam was opened without warning in 2024, Amballur and Puthukkad bore the brunt of floods, he said.
How will the water flowing down from the eastern hills and low-lying areas make its way westward after being obstructed by the Amballur and Puthukkad flyovers, built in close proximity to each other?
This is the question raised by the KSSP activists, who conducted a study of the region.
“The ecological implications of altering the existing drainage pattern needs to be studied comprehensively before the project design is finalised.

stories.headline: Madras High Court begins hearing Tamil Nadu CM Vijay’s plea to reject election petitions
stories.title: Madras High Court begins hearing Tamil Nadu CM Vijay’s plea to reject election petitions
stories.summary: Justice V. Lakshminarayanan accepts a request made by senior counsel Srinath Sridevan to hear the four applications one after the other
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Madras High Court on Monday (October 5, 2026) commenced hearing arguments on an application filed by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to reject an election petition filed by a voter, S. Dinesh, challenging his victory from the Perambur Assembly constituency this year.

Justice V. Lakshminarayanan is seized of three election petitions, including the one filed by another voter, T.N. Lakshmi Narasimhan, and Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam’s losing candidate R.D. Shekar, filed against the Chief Minister’s victory in Perambur by a margin of 53,715 votes.

Apart from these three, one more election petition had been filed by DMK candidate S. Inigo Irudayaraj, challenging Mr. Vijay’s victory from the Tiruchi East Assembly constituency, which he had vacated after contesting and winning from both constituencies.

The judge accepted a request made by senior counsel Srinath Sridevan, representing the Chief Minister, to hear the arguments one after another on the applications filed for rejecting each of the four election petitions, as there were certain differences in each case despite overlapping pleadings.

He began hearing the plea to reject Mr. Dinesh’s election petition – filed through the latter’s counsel V.R. Shanmuganathan – first, and decided to take up the application to reject Mr. Narasimhan’s election petition thereafter, since they got numbered one after another.

Senior counsel Gopal Sankaranarayanan, assisted by Pranjal Agarwal and Dixita Gohil, commenced his arguments to reject the first election petition and contended that there was no basis for the allegation of the Chief Minister not having made full and proper disclosure of his assets and liabilities.

He took the court through the evolution of the legal requirement of candidates disclosing their assets, beginning from the 170th Law Commission report submitted in 1999, which recommended such a measure for the first time and also a catena of judgments that were delivered on the issue thereafter.

However, since Mr. Sankaranarayanan could not conclude his arguments on Monday and sought time to continue his submissions some other day, the judge decided to hear him on Tuesday as well, before granting an opportunity to the election petitioner’s counsel Mr. Shanmuganathan to respond.

stories.headline: Odisha government announces to hold student union election after a gap of eight years
stories.title: Odisha government announces to hold student union election after a gap of eight years
stories.summary: Process of elections to be completed in next 10 days; will begin from October 7 and come to end on October 16, 2026
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Odisha government on Monday (Octobeer 5, 2026) announced that student union elections will be held on higher education campuses after a gap of eight years.
The elections will be completed within the next 10 days.
Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi approved conducting student union elections, which involves massive security arrangement in view of possible violence on campuses.

Speaking after his meeting with the Odisha Chief Minister, State Higher Education Minister Suryabanshi Suraj said, “the detailed timeline and complete information will be provided by the department very soon.
A final decision has been taken to hold the elections before the Dussehra holidays, and colleges will issue their own notifications on the October 7, 2026.
Nominations will be filed on the October 9, and the elections will be held on the October 15 and the oath-taking ceremony will be held on the morning of October 16.”
“We believe that conducting these elections is important because today’s students and student leaders are the future leaders of Odisha.

This process will help them understand democratic responsibilities, the importance of democracy, and constitutional values, preparing them to take up leadership roles in the future,” said Mr. Suryabanshi.
Stating that the this is a significant step, the Minister informed “student union elections had been suspended since 2017.
We had also promised in our election manifesto that these elections would be conducted.
After formation of our government in 2024, we spent 2025 addressing various issues on campuses, and in 2026 we are now moving ahead with student union elections.”
He said to ensure peaceful and orderly elections, the Supreme Court’s 2005 verdict and the recommendations of the J. M Lyngdoh Committee, which were followed earlier, will continue to be implemented.

stories.headline: Congress, allies seeking Bangladesh-like regime change: Rajnath
stories.title: Congress, allies seeking Bangladesh-like regime change: Rajnath
stories.summary: Lucknow, Oct 16: Union Minister Rajnath Singh on Friday lashed out at the Congress and its allies over the protests in the national capital, accusing them of seeking a regime change along the lines of Bangladesh and using the energy of youth to spread "anarchy". Addressing a press conference here, Singh asserted that democracy does not give anyone the licence to create disorder or undermine the credibility of constitutional institutions. "It appears that the Congress and its political allies, directly and through their supporting organisations, are trying to use the energy of the youth to fuel political confrontation and spread anarchy instead of channelling it towards constructive work and nation-building," he said. "The youth of the country are being made pawns in the politics of anarchy," he stated. Singh alleged that the Congress and its allies want a change of government in India along the lines of Bangladesh. "They openly say at press conferences that they have drawn inspiration from Bangladesh for regime change, while another speaks openly about bringing down the government. This makes it clear that their only agenda is to dismantle democratic institutions and set the country on fire," he said referring to the uprising in Bangladesh in 2024 that toppled the Sheikh Hasina government. The defence minister said the use of terms such as "regime change" showed that the opposition's campaign was not about electoral reforms or issues related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. His remarks come amid massive protests in the national capital by opposition parties and civil society groups demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the SIR process. Opposition leaders have alleged that the exercise lacks transparency and could exclude eligible voters. Referring to the Supreme Court's observations on Thursday, Singh said Gandhi and his allies need to understand that democracy does not permit attempts to create anarchy, undermine constitutional institutions or obstruct India's development. "Respecting the law is also essential to maintaining law and order. India's democratic institutions cannot be sacrificed at the altar of political self-interest," he said. Singh added that falsehoods, anger, attempts to malign institutions and political opportunism could not obstruct India's development. He advised Gandhi to respect the people's mandate and introspect on his political role instead of pursuing what he called "politics of destruction" in the name of protecting democracy. "India's future is everyone's responsibility. We must choose the path of dialogue and nation-building, not confrontation," Singh said.

stories.headline: Pinarayi Vijayan moves Supreme Court against FIR order in CMRL bribery case
stories.title: Pinarayi Vijayan moves Supreme Court against FIR order in CMRL bribery case
stories.summary: Pinarayi Vijayan moves Supreme Court against FIR order in CMRL bribery case
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: The challenge tests whether corruption suspects can claim a hearing before FIR registration.

Former Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan on Friday moved the Supreme Court against a Kerala High Court order directing the registration of a first information report (FIR) in the alleged CMRL bribery case, news agency Press Trust of India reported.
Vijayan has also sought protection from coercive action.
The Supreme Court said it would hear the matter after reopening on October 26 following the Dussehra break.
According to PTI, senior advocate Sidharth Luthra, appearing for Vijayan, sought an urgent hearing before a bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi.
He told the bench that an FIR had been registered in the case and requested protection for Vijayan.
The Chief Justice said the matter would be heard when the court reopens.
He also said a bench could be constituted during the holidays next week, subject to the availability of judges.

The Kerala High Court had on Thursday dismissed applications filed by Vijayan, his daughter Veena T and her husband P. A Mohamed Riyas seeking permission to appeal against an October 9 order by a single judge directing the registration of an FIR against them.
A division bench rejected the applications, holding that “an accused in a corruption case has no legal right to be heard before registering the FIR”.
It said the related appeals were also dismissed as a consequence.
Vijayan, Veena and Riyas had argued in their appeals that the single judge did not hear them before issuing the direction to register the FIR.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court issued notices over an opposition petition challenging electoral roll revisions.
Sanjay Raut's participation remains provisional pending an explanation of his conduct.

The Supreme Court has said Shiv Sena-UBT leader Sanjay Raut will have to explain his conduct while issuing notices to the Election Commission and its chief, Gyanesh Kumar, over a petition alleging irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, news agency Press Trust of India reported.
The petition was filed by Congress leader Rahul Gandhi along with 12 other opposition leaders, including Raut.
The court said it was provisionally accepting the petition on Raut's behalf, subject to his explanation.
A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi said on Thursday: "In WP (C) No 1351/2026 (Item 25, filed by Gandhi), the petition on behalf of petitioner no.
6 (Raut) is entertained on a provisional basis, subject to his explaining his conduct."
During the hearing, the Chief Justice, without naming anyone, said: "We will ask one of the petitioners about his conduct on the next date of hearing."

The Chief Justice also responded strongly when some lawyers alleged that Gandhi and other opposition leaders, who marched to the Supreme Court on October 12, had been trying to browbeat the judiciary.
"Nobody can browbeat us (judiciary)," the Chief Justice said.
"We are not sitting in ivory towers.
We know what statements they are making outside and what they are saying in court.

article_sentences: The proposed increase could be around half the magnitude of the cumulative 7.5% hike implemented in May, the only period when retail fuel prices rose in response to the war in the Middle East.

Such an increase could push retail inflation to 6.2% in the October-December quarter and 6.5% in the first three months of 2027, both exceeding the Reserve Bank of India’s inflation target range of 2-6%, it said.
Oxford Economics’ projections are higher than the central bank’s estimates.
In its monetary policy review earlier this month, the RBI projected inflation at 6% for the October-December quarter, easing to 5.7% in January-March.
Oxford Economics expects price pressures to intensify next year, forecasting inflation at 5.4% for the financial year ending March, compared with the RBI’s projection of 5.2%.
If authorities do not announce a fuel price increase in November, Oxford Economics’ inflation projections could decline by 10-30 basis points in the coming quarters, the report added.

Inflation would nevertheless remain elevated, potentially prompting the RBI to raise interest rates by 25 basis points each at its December and February policy meetings, following a quarter-point increase in October.
Inflation rose to 5.54% in September, its highest level since late 2024, from 4.83% in August.
Hermann Prasad said the RBI’s recent measures in the currency market should help contain rupee volatility.
However, elevated oil prices and persistent external financing pressures mean intervention alone is unlikely to ensure lasting currency stability.

She also said widening protests over allegations of electoral malpractice were unlikely to materially affect economic growth, as disruption had largely remained confined to Delhi and was too limited to have a significant impact.

Separately, aviation minister Ram Mohan Naidu said that discussions are underway with airlines to ensure that ticket prices are kept reasonable, which is a challenging task given the unstable jet fuel prices.

stories.title: SC issues notice to Congress, Rahul Gandhi over march to court, posts against CJI
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 15: The Supreme Court on Thursday issued notice to the Congress, Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders on a plea seeking restrictions on political demonstrations in court premises following the Opposition’s march to the apex court on October 12 and social media posts targeting Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant. A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi sought responses to the petition filed by four lawyers. Senior Advocate Gaurav Bhatia, appearing for the petitioners, argued that demonstrations within court premises amounted to an attempt to intimidate the judiciary. “Nobody can browbeat the judiciary,” the CJI observed. “We are not sitting in ivory towers. We know what statements they are making outside and what they are saying in Court. We know everything,” he said. The petition also sought criminal contempt action against the Congress’s Kerala unit over an X post that told the CJI to resign and said the party would find his replacement. However, the bench declined to issue notice on the contempt plea at this stage. “No contempt today. We are only issuing notice. Let us see what the response is, and then we will take it forward,” the CJI said, according to Bar & Bench. The plea also named Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav among the respondents.

In its order, the bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi said that the petition was being provisionally entertained at Raut's instance, subject to him explaining his conduct.

Incidentally, Attorney General R Venkataramani granted consent yesterday to the Supreme Court Bar Association to initiate criminal contempt proceedings against Raut over his comments concerning the judiciary and CJI Surya Kant.

During Thursday's hearing, the CJI had remarked that one of the petitioners would have to explain his conduct.
The CJI also observed that the judges were aware of statements being made outside the courtroom and were not living in "ivory towers".

While giving consent for criminal contempt proceedings, the Attorney General stated that Raut's statement on judges playing badminton with Ministers was false, and cited a Delhi High Court order which established this.
The AG also said that Raut's comments lowered the dignity of the judiciary and were scandalous in nature.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday (October 5, 2026) asked the Delhi High Court to consider a plea by 11 members of the Delhi Gymkhana Club, who had challenged the Centre's decision to take over the club's 27.3-acre premises and the subsequent eviction proceedings.

A Bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana was told by senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for the members, that the Delhi High Court had refused to entertain their plea on the ground that only the club could challenge the Centre's decision.
Mr. Singh said the High Court had asked the members to get a clarification from the Supreme Court that they could also move the plea there.
The Court permitted them to move the High Court, subject to objections that may be raised by the other side regarding maintainability and other legal oppositions.

Mr. Singh, appearing for the 11 members, had earlier told the Bench that a Central government-nominated committee was presently managing the club, and that it could not fight a legal battle with the government.

On September 3, 2026, the Centre, in a separate case, told the Delhi High Court that it would not take any coercive action until September 16, 2026, against the club in relation to its eviction from the premises on Safdarjung Road.

The High Court was hearing pleas by club member Vijay Khurana and others, seeking a stay on the June 29, 2026, show-cause notice for eviction issued to the club's management by an estate officer of the Land and Development Office (L&DO).

Vipin Aggarwal and ten other club members, in their petition filed through lawyer Nitin Saluja, sought the quashing of the resumption notification issued by the L&DO on May 22, 2026, and the show-cause notice issued by the estate officer on June 29, 2026.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Thursday, October 15, issued notice to the Election Commission of India (ECI), Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi on a petition filed by Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders challenging decisions related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
During the hearing, Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant said that the court could not be intimidated by political processions, observing, “Nobody can browbeat us.”

A bench comprising CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi issued notice on the petition, which raises allegations of irregularities in the ECI's functioning and seeks the suspension of the SIR exercise, including in poll-bound states.
The bench said it would examine the responses and hear petitions challenging the SIR process state-wise, rather than clubbing all the matters together.

The court's observations came amid arguments by senior advocate Gaurav Bhatia, who referred to a memorandum signed by around 200 lawyers expressing concern over the October 12 march led by Rahul Gandhi and other Opposition leaders to the Supreme Court premises.
Bhatia argued that the gathering amounted to an attempt to pressure the judiciary and said that the incident had caused concern among lawyers.
The CJI responded, “These are feeble attempts that nobody takes note of.”
“We are not sitting in ivory towers.
We know what statements they make outside and what they say in court.
We know everything,” the CJI said.
The bench also clarified that issuing notice on the INDIA bloc's petition did not mean that the court approved of the political leaders' conduct.
“We would also ask one of the petitioners about his conduct,” the CJI said.

(This matter doesn't pertain to my domain)," Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant said on Monday, when asked about protests against the CEC in Delhi over the past few days and the associated restrictions.
The CJI was interacting with reporters on the sidelines of an event to commemorate the 33rd anniversary of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) at Vigyan Bhawan here.
The last few days have seen protests against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar in different parts of Delhi.
Over the weekend, the capital turned into a fortress, with massive deployment of security personnel, closure of 45 metro stations and intensive checks at the city's border points.
Thousands of protesters, including Cockroach Janta Party leaders and former chief ministers, were detained.
The CJI, when asked about these protests and the restrictions on movement, said the matter was related to law and order.
"Ye mera mudda nahin hai," he said.

stories.headline: India GDP to grow 7.1-7.3% in FY27 on private investment revival: Deloitte
stories.title: India GDP to grow 7.1-7.3% in FY27 on private investment revival: Deloitte
stories.summary: The Indian economy is expected to grow by 7.1-7.3 per cent in the current fiscal, with a sustained revival in private investment providing an additional source of demand, Deloitte India said on Friday. However, geopolitical tensions, volatile energy prices and trade disruptions pose risks to the growth outlook, it added. Deloitte India Economist Rumki Majumdar said over the past decade, India's growth has rested on resilient household spending and sustained investment push in public infrastructure. Businesses now have better connectivity, healthier balance sheets, and higher capacity utilisation, which strengthens the case for expansion. "The question is whether these conditions will encourage private investment to play a larger role in boosting growth in the coming years. Recent indicators offer grounds for optimism. Gross fixed capital formation grew by 11.9 per cent in the first quarter of FY 2026-27, its fastest expansion in four years," Majumdar said. Deloitte Economic Outlook
